changes.before: indicates that the labor market remains strong but that growth of economic activity has slowed from its solid rate in the fourth quarter.
changes.after: indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity rose at a solid rate.

changes.before: Payroll employment was little changed in February, but job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.after: Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.

changes.before: Recent indicators point to slower growth of household spending and business fixed investment in the first quarter.
changes.after: Growth of household spending and business fixed investment slowed in the first quarter.

changes.before: On a 12-month basis, overall inflation has declined, largely as a result of lower energy prices; inflation for items other than food and energy remains near 2 percent.
changes.after: On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have declined and are running below 2 percent.

parsed.rationale: The growth assessment was upgraded while core inflation is now described as below 2 percent, roughly offsetting signals. The policy guidance, including the 'patient' language and the rate target, is unchanged.

spans.quote: indicates that the labor market remains strong but that growth of economic activity has slowed from its solid rate in the fourth quarter.
Payroll employment was little changed in February, but job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
Recent indicators point to slower growth of household spending and business fixed investment in the first quarter.
On a 12-month basis, overall inflation has declined, largely as a result of lower energy prices; inflation for items other than food and energy remains near 2 percent.
Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; John C. Williams, Vice Chairman;
indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity rose at a solid rate.
Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
Growth of household spending and business fixed investment slowed in the first quarter.
On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have declined and are running below 2 percent.
Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair;
